_comment: The board vocabulary that ships with the command tier. `fleet commands sync` renders it to `.claude/board-guidance.json`: every command rewritten to the repository's namespace and every entry naming a command the repository's set does not carry dropped, so the board names exactly the commands the repository has. Generated — edit the source in the package's `commandtree/`, never the rendered copy.

howLabel.board: a page hands it to you
howLabel.typed: you type it to start a session

catalogue: A question, research, or you do not know yet whether it is work. Loads nothing heavy and changes nothing.
The front door for anything a person files: a short interview that turns it into one decision-ready write-up.
Anything new that might be built. It classifies it — program, slice, PRD, task, bug or idea — and files it.
The gate every filed issue passes through before the fleet may build it.
The gate every fix passes on its way out: proves the issue is closed at the pull request's head, then merges or returns it.
Work through everything that is waiting on you and nobody else.
Commit and open a pull request, or ship it on green checks.
A checklist-driven audit of one area, filed as findings.
Check one shipped promise on a named environment with the platform's own evidence, and land the scenario and its result.
Re-grade the QA agent's passes from their evidence, approve changed expected results, and check each week that a planted bug turns a scenario red.
Stand behind one property of the running product: measure it every cycle and hand reds to the fleet.
Ride along while a person uses the product, and collect what they do not like.
Park something early, without committing to it.
File a bug with what was seen and how to reproduce it.
Prove a filed bug with a failing test.
Fix a bug test-first through to a green pull request.
File a small piece of work that needs no PRD.
Build a small task through to a green pull request.
Register a durable part of the system.

Give a new repository with no code its first running code: a hello-world web service on a fixed port, a unit test, lint, a build and CI, by one pull request the verify gate certifies. Typed, or started from Set up the code on the Set up page.
Describe an existing code base into the knowledge base, one step a session: components, then capabilities and rules confirmed with you, then areas and journeys.

Describe one part of a repository from the Knowledge page: it reads every file the part owns, asks you to confirm what it promises through the fleet's question channel, and lands the result. Never typed.
Bring the architecture documents back in line with the code.
Write or refresh a page's experience contract.
Make a mockup for one surface, render and critique it, then ask a person to approve it.
Change a page against its experience contract, through to a pull request.
Turn recurring friction from past runs into fixes to the procedures behind it.
A result someone gets has no home yet. Adds a row to the program register.
Work backwards from a program: what has to exist for this to be true? Produces the gaps and their build order.
Shape a program that is only a row, from its page, through the fleet's question channel. Never typed.
Name a shaped program's proof, or honestly none, through the fleet's question channel. Never typed.
One delivery cycle on a program already in execution: releases what is ready, chases stalls, and asks you about anything blocking.
Say which proof counts — the run that shows the whole thread works, not one lane of it.
Close a program whose proof has held.
Cut a planning slice inside a program.
Change what a cut waits on, which run proves it, or the sentence that says when it is done.
Refine a slice cut from a brief, from its page, through the fleet's question channel. Never typed.
Author a PRD inside a slice. This is where a promise turns into work.
Fill a PRD stub from its page, through the fleet's question channel, and land it drafted. Never typed.
Design a drafted PRD on the fleet, just in time.
Technical and experience design for a drafted PRD.
Implementation plans for a designed PRD.
Build a planned PRD through to a green pull request.
Audit what shipped against what the PRD promised.
Drop a PRD that should not happen, with the reason recorded.

Say which proof counts. It writes nothing when no honest proof exists yet.
Close it, once its proof has held.
Cut a new slice inside this program.

Change what this cut waits on, which run proves it, or when it is done.
Cut a sibling slice next to this one.
Drop a PRD that should not happen, with the reason recorded.

Build it through to a green pull request.
Drop a PRD that should not happen, with the reason recorded.

Change what a cut waits on, which run proves it, or when it is done.
Cut the slices a program has none of.
